content.comment_body: Facing the same issue, receiving an 'unable to read card' message. Is it possible to use an empty, formatted card? Diagnostics are showing an 'SD card read/write error'.

Recently, I programmed a large project using 32 memory cards for four networked controllers. I used KINGSTON 8GB cards straight out of the packaging and had no issues—all cards worked immediately. My recommendation is to use genuine branded memory cards, not cheap or counterfeit ones. These cards simplified programming and allowed easy transfer; if a user alters the program or loses track of timer settings, a reboot restores my original version automatically.
When transferring modified programs using 'Copy to SD card', it's crucial to ensure proper checks. However, using write protection on the SD card prevents unintentional overwriting.
Yes, the SD cards are write-protected. Users typically adjust timer settings, and I've assigned clear names to assist them. These steps reduce unnecessary support visits and keep users satisfied.
My issue is resolved. Formatting the SD card completely in FAT32 (not quick format) made everything work perfectly.
